Monica / Ben — quick legal note on signing authority and subprocessor acknowledgement:

1) Signing authority: per our current delegation matrix, DPAs and standard MSAs under $1M ARR-equivalent can be signed by the VP of Legal or the CRO. For countersignature we typically use: Rishi Malhotra, VP Legal (for routine DPAs) or Priya Natarajan, CRO (for strategic/enterprise with bespoke SLAs). If the counterparty requires an authorized officer signature block (CEO/CFO), we need a written escalation to leadership — that slows the timeline.

2) Subprocessor snapshot: Legal prefers to include a clause that allows Redwood to provide a frozen snapshot of the subprocessor list as of execution; after execution, notifications for new subprocessors are communicated via the portal. For high-regulation customers we add an attestation addendum.

3) Redlines: I'm attaching the latest redline summary I prepared after Laura's file review. The main open redline is data residency/transfer language — propose a short carrier clause and optional SCCs link in the DPA.

I approve the proposed DocuSign flow (initiate -> LumenTech steps -> Redwood countersign). Ben — ensure the envelope requires emailed record of final envelope status (completed) and retains the audit trail in our G-Drive contract folder.

Rishi Malhotra
VP, Legal — Redwood Inference
